chunks: And through his chain of narration, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who saw a bird and followed it until it landed on a tree, then a man came and caught it. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'To the eye belongs what it saw, and to the hand belongs what it caught.'

key_terms.لِلْعَيْنِ مَا رَأَتْ: To the eye belongs what it saw (principle of visual acquisition)
key_terms.لِلْيَدِ مَا أَخَذَتْ: To the hand belongs what it caught (principle of physical possession)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal principle regarding ownership of game through sight and capture?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) articulates the dual criteria for valid acquisition in hunting: visual tracking establishes the initial right, while physical capture consummates ownership. This principle, foundational in Shia fiqh, distinguishes between the preparatory act of sighting and the definitive act of taking, ensuring clarity in property rights during the hunt. It reflects the juristic emphasis on tangible evidence and clear boundaries in transactional and possessive rights.
